kjv: When a man shall make a singular vow
mine: When anyone makes a special vow
note: yafli' neder means "makes an extraordinary or special vow". "Singular" now means "single".

kjv: None devoted, which shall be devoted of men, shall be redeemed; but shall surely be put to death
mine: No one devoted ... from among mankind, shall be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death
note: cherem of persons means those placed under the ban of destruction (e.g., in war or by judicial sentence). Both translations are literal. The KJV's "of men" leaves unclear whether it means a person someone has vowed or a person condemned. Context: a person under the ban of destruction (medium confidence). Cherem of persons denotes those placed under the ban of destruction, in war (1 Sam 15) or by judicial sentence (Exod 22:19). Since 27:1-8 lets vowed persons be redeemed, 27:29 is best read of persons already under the ban, not private vows. The rendering follows the Hebrew closely, as ESV and NRSV do. Other possible meanings: (1) a person devoted to God by an individual's vow must die — read by some into the Jephthah story (Judg 11:30-39), but most reject it since 27:1-8 provides redemption; (2) a person already condemned to death by a court cannot be valued or ransomed — Mishnah Arakhin, Rashi.
